name: kb_793_Normalized

https:__kubernetesjsonschema_dev_master_.description: LocalObjectReference contains enough information to let you locate the referenced object inside the same namespace.

name.description: Name of the referent. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

schema.description: Represents a Rados Block Device mount that lasts the lifetime of a pod. RBD volumes support ownership management and SELinux relabeling.

fsType.description: Filesystem type of the volume that you want to mount. Tip: Ensure that the filesystem type is supported by the host operating system. Examples: "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". Implicitly inferred to be "ext4" if unspecified. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes#rbd

image.description: The rados image name. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/rbd/README.md#how-to-use-it

keyring.description: Keyring is the path to key ring for RBDUser. Default is /etc/ceph/keyring. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/rbd/README.md#how-to-use-it

monitors.description: A collection of Ceph monitors. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/rbd/README.md#how-to-use-it

pool.description: The rados pool name. Default is rbd. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/rbd/README.md#how-to-use-it

readOnly.description: ReadOnly here will force the ReadOnly setting in VolumeMounts. Defaults to false. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/rbd/README.md#how-to-use-it

secretRef.description: SecretRef is name of the authentication secret for RBDUser. If provided overrides keyring. Default is nil. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/rbd/README.md#how-to-use-it

user.description: The rados user name. Default is admin. More info: https://examples.k8s.io/volumes/rbd/README.md#how-to-use-it

description: The pod will mount an RBD volume using the image **my‑rbd‑image** with an ext4 filesystem. The Ceph monitors are reachable at 10.0.0.1:6789, 10.0.0.2:6789 and 10.0.0.3:6789, and the volume resides in the default **rbd** pool. Access to the RBD cluster is performed as the **admin** user, using the keyring located at **/etc/ceph/keyring**; the authentication secret is supplied via the Kubernetes secret named **rbd‑secret**. The volume is mounted read‑write (ReadOnly is false).
